journal.colonyjournal.guide.intro.title: What it is
journal.colonyjournal.guide.intro.body:
The Colony Journal explains your MineColonies colony in plain words: what works, what is missing and what to do about it.
- [chain] Links: a map of which building feeds which.
- [redstone_torch] Problems: a list of what is wrong, worst first.
- [bricks] Buildings: every building with its workers.
- [gold_ingot] Economy: the colony treasury and the tax.
- [emerald] Market: buy goods and trade with other players.
- [clock] Statistics: all colonies on the server side by side.
Start with the Overview tab: it shows the state of the colony as traffic lights and tells you what to do next.
# Colours mean the same everywhere
- [color:55CC66] Green: everything is fine.
- [color:E0C040] Yellow: needs attention, but nothing is broken yet.
- [color:E05050] Red: a problem. Fix it first.
Every tab has a ? button in its top corner. It opens this guide at the matching topic.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.steps.title: First steps
journal.colonyjournal.guide.steps.body:
A short checklist for a new colony. Work through it from top to bottom.
- [bell] Town hall: the heart of the colony. Nothing works without it.
- [chest] Warehouse and a courier: goods are stored in the warehouse and carried between buildings by the courier.
- [red_bed] Residences: every citizen needs a bed. When the citizen limit is reached the colony stops growing.
- [bricks] Builder: he builds every other hut you place.
- [iron_hoe] Food: a farmer, and a cook so that nobody starves.
- [golden_apple] Hospital: heals sick and wounded citizens.
- [iron_sword] Guard tower: guards protect the colony from raids.
- [iron_pickaxe] Producers: miner, lumberjack, farmer and friends. They bring in the coins (see Economy).
The Problems tab lists the basic buildings you are still missing. Come back to the Overview from time to time: it always names the next step.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.overview.bod:
The first page of the journal. It answers two questions: how is my colony doing, and what should I do now?
# Four traffic lights
- [chain] Supply chains: green when every building gets what it needs. Red when a basic building or a key producer is missing.
- [gold_ingot] Treasury and taxes: red when the treasury is in debt or about to run out, yellow when the tax is higher than the citizens like.
- [golden_apple] Citizen happiness: how content the citizens are (0 to 10) and what the tax does to their mood.
- [emerald] Trade and prosperity: whether your producers make goods to sell, and how prosperous the colony is.
Click a card to open the tab with the details.
# What to do next
Up to five actions, most important first, made from the real state of your colony. Click one to jump to the right place. Actions about a building show it on the Links map.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.links.title: Supply chains
journal.colonyjournal.guide.links.body:
The Links tab shows one supply chain at a time, so nothing gets tangled.
# Chains
- [chain] The strip at the top has one button per chain: metal, tools, wood, stone, crops, meat, dyes, the basic buildings and the rest. A coloured dot shows how the chain is doing and the numbers say how many of its buildings work.
- [color:55CC66] Green dot: the chain is fine.
- [color:E0C040] Yellow dot: a building has no worker or is not finished.
- [color:E05050] Red dot: a producer is missing or idle while someone waits for its goods.
The journal opens the first chain that has a problem.
# Buildings
- [frame:ok] Green: working.
- [frame:partial] Yellow: partly staffed.
- [frame:no_worker] Orange: built, but nobody works there.
- [frame:unbuilt] Red: the hut stands, but it is not built yet.
- [frame:absent] Grey dashed card: you do not have this building. It is shown on purpose, so you see what is missing.
The name is next to the icon. x3 means three buildings of that type, 1/2 means one worker for two places.
# Arrows
Arrows go from left to right: from the building that makes the goods to the building that needs them.
- [line:6FE07F] Green arrow: the goods are delivered.
- [line:E05050] Red arrow: the building waits for goods from a producer that is missing or idle.
- [line:E0A030] Dashed amber arrow: the same, but the goods are optional.
- [line:8C8C8C] Grey arrow: nobody waits for it yet, because the receiving building is not built.
A short word on an arrow says what is delivered, when there is room for it. Hover over any arrow to read it.
# Using the tab
Click a building: its arrows light up, the others fade, and the panel at the bottom says in plain words what to do. Click empty space to clear the selection. When a chain is bigger than the window, drag it with the mouse or use the wheel. The Legend button shows this key at any time.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.problems.bod:
Everything the journal found wrong in your colony, from the most to the least serious.
- [barrier] Red stripe, a problem: a basic building is missing, or a building waits for something nobody can supply. Fix these first.
- [glowstone_dust] Yellow stripe, attention: a building has no worker, the citizen limit is reached or a supply chain is broken.
- [light_blue_dye] Blue stripe, a note: not urgent, for example a hut that is not built yet.
When a building asks for an item, the journal tells you who could supply it, for example: Guard Tower requests Iron Sword - Blacksmith: not built.
Click a row to show the building on the Links map. When the list is empty, all supply chains are complete.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.buildings.bo:
One row per building. The stripe on the left has the same colours as the map.
- Level: current level / highest level. Higher levels work better and earn more.
- Workers: citizens working there / places. Green = full, yellow = some, orange = nobody.
- Requests: items the building is waiting for. The Problems tab says who could supply them.
- Position: where the hut stands. Shown when the window is wide enough.
A building without workers earns nothing. Open its hut and assign a citizen, or build more residences so that new citizens arrive.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.economy.body:
The colony has one shared treasury, counted in coins. Income is paid in and upkeep is paid out once per game day.
# Where the coins come from
- [iron_pickaxe] Producers: gatherers, processors and crafters (miner, farmer, smeltery, blacksmith, cook...). Each working worker makes 30 + 15 x level coins of value per day, at most 90 x level per building. The colony keeps the tax share of that.
- [coin] Trade: surplus goods are sold automatically, see the Market.
# Where the coins go
- [bell] Service buildings cost upkeep: warehouse, courier, town hall and the consumers (builder, guards, hospital, library...). A service building costs 2 + 2 x level coins a day, the town hall 3 + 3 x level.
- Residences and other buildings outside the chains cost nothing and earn nothing.
# The tax
The tax is a percentage from 0 to 50 (12 by default): the colony keeps that share of what its producers make. Set it with the slider on the Economy tab and press Confirm. Only the owner and the officers can change it.
# A worked example
A level 2 farmer with 2 workers makes 2 x (30 + 15 x 2) = 120. A level 2 lumberjack with 1 worker makes 60. Together 180. At 12%% tax the colony earns 21 coins a day.
Upkeep: town hall level 2 = 9, warehouse level 1 = 4, guard tower level 1 = 4, together 17. Net: +4 coins a day.
# Debt
If the treasury runs dry it can sink to -500 coins at most. Debt makes citizens unhappy.
These numbers are the defaults. The server owner can change them in the mod config.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.happiness.bo:
Citizens work better and stay longer when they are happy. The journal shows happiness on a scale from 0 to 10.
# The comfortable tax rate
Every colony size has a tax rate that citizens accept: 40 - 0.4 x citizens, but never below 10 or above 40. With 10 citizens it is 36%%, with 50 citizens 20%%, from 75 citizens on 10%%.
- [color:55CC66] At or below that rate citizens are content. The lower the tax, the bigger the small bonus (up to +10%% mood).
- [color:E05050] Above it they grow unhappy. At the highest allowed tax the mood factor falls to 50%%.
The white marker on the tax slider shows the comfortable rate.
# Growing colonies
The bigger the colony, the lower the comfortable rate. A tax that was fine early on can start to annoy the citizens later, so look at the marker now and then.
# Debt
An empty treasury hurts the mood as well, a little more with every day of debt (for up to eight days).
Food, housing, safety and the other things citizens care about come from MineColonies itself. The journal only adds the tax and the debt.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.market.title: Market
journal.colonyjournal.guide.market.body:
The Market has two parts, chosen with the buttons at the top.
# Colony goods
- Every working producer building makes goods: workers x (2 + level) x (1 + 0.5 x prosperity) units a day.
- Colonies sell their goods by themselves. You buy x1, x8 or x64 with the coins of your colony.
- Every item has a base price. The prosperity of the seller scales it between 0.8 and 1.7 times.
- Stock is limited to 48 + 16 x (sum of the levels of the buildings that make the item). What does not fit is sold automatically into the treasury at 35%% of the retail price: that is the trade income on the Economy tab.
- The seller colony receives the price minus a 5%% fee. If both colonies belong to the same owner, nobody is paid and the whole price vanishes, so goods are no free money.
# Prosperity
Prosperity (0 to 100%%) = 40%% building levels (average level 5 counts as full) + 40%% happiness + 20%% colony size (80 citizens count as full). It raises prices and output.
# Player offers
- Players put items on the market at their own price, from 1 to 1000000 coins. Buy with the Buy button, take your own offer back with Withdraw.
- To sell: hold the item in your main hand and open the journal with the J key (not with the journal item, it would occupy your hand), type a price and press Post.
- The seller colony gets the price minus 5%%. You cannot buy your own offers or offers of your own colonies.
- A colony can have only a limited number of offers (8 by default).
Buying needs owner or officer rights in the colony.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.stats.title: Statistics
journal.colonyjournal.guide.stats.body:
A table of every colony on the server. Your own colonies are highlighted in gold.
- Click a column header to sort, click again to reverse the order.
- The mouse wheel scrolls up and down, Shift + wheel scrolls sideways.
- Hover over a row to see all its numbers.
- Happiness is 0 to 10. Income and upkeep are coins per day. Day is the colony's own day counter.
Use it to see how you compare. Colonies with a higher prosperity also charge more for their goods on the Market.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.glossary.bod:
- [coin] Coin: the money of the journal's economy. Buildings earn and spend it, goods are bought with it.
- Treasury: the shared pile of coins of one colony.
- Producer: a gatherer, processor or crafter building. It earns coins while it has workers.
- Service building: costs upkeep. The town hall, warehouse, courier and the consumers (builder, guards, hospital...).
- Upkeep: the coins a service building costs every day.
- Tax rate: the share of the producers' output that the colony keeps.
- Comfortable rate (tolerable rate): the tax citizens accept at the current colony size. It falls as the colony grows.
- Prosperity: a score from 0 to 100%% made of building levels, happiness and colony size. It raises prices and output.
- Stock: the goods a colony holds for sale.
- Surplus: goods above the stock limit. They are sold automatically for a low price.
- Settlement: the daily accounting at the end of each colony day.
journal.colonyjournal.guide.controls.bod:
- J: open the journal for the colony around you (you can change the key in Controls).
- Journal item (right click): the same, but the item stays in your hand. Use the J key when you want to sell the item in your hand.
- Mouse wheel: scroll lists. On the Links map it moves the map, with Shift sideways.
- Drag: move the Links map.
- Esc or E: close the journal. E does nothing while you are typing in a text box.
- ? in the top corner of a tab: open this guide at the matching topic.
- Hover over anything for a tooltip.
# Tips
- Start at the Overview.
- The Economy, Market and Statistics tabs refresh by themselves while they are open.
- They need the mod on the server too.
